mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕'责任'展开，涵盖守约与信义（Reading）、毕业致辞·责任的分量（Extended reading）、勇于担当·别急于责怪他人（Grammar and usage）和承认错误的勇气（Integrated skills）四个板块——责任与担当是高考应用文'演讲/书信'类的高频立意，也是雅思品格与社会类议论文的核心命题。

subTopics.title: 守约与信义
subTopics.desc: 课文《二十年后》核心：一位警察在夜里 on the beat，一个人为了二十年前的一个约定 kept an appointment——信义，是一个人对自己诺言的责任。

prompts.task: 你校英文报以 "A Promise Kept" 为题征稿。请你写一篇短文，讲述一次你信守承诺的经历，内容包括：1. 事情经过；2. 你的感悟。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Two years ago, I promised my grandmother that I would visit her every month after she moved to the countryside. It sounded easy at the time.

But life grew busy, and one cold weekend I almost gave up the trip. Then I remembered the appointment we had made, and how her face lit up each time I appeared at the door. So I went. At the appointed time she was already waiting at the gate, and though two years had passed, our bond had barely changed.

Keeping a small promise is not always convenient, but it is what makes us people others can rely on. A person's word, I have learned, is a quiet form of responsibility — and the easiest one to break.

prompts.task: Some people believe that keeping one's promises is one of the most important qualities a person can have. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Reliability is often praised, and some argue that keeping one's promises ranks among the most valuable of all human qualities. I largely agree, because a person's word underpins the trust on which relationships, work and society itself depend, even if rare circumstances can justify breaking it.

The central reason is trust. Every serious relationship — friendship, marriage, employment, citizenship — rests on the assumption that people will do what they say. A friend who keeps promises can be relied on in a crisis; an employee who meets commitments is given responsibility and opportunity; a government that honours its pledges earns the confidence of its people. Where promises are broken casually, cooperation collapses, because no one can plan around another's word. In this sense, keeping promises is not merely one virtue among many but the foundation that makes other virtues useful.

There is, admittedly, a sensible limit. A promise made in ignorance, or one that would cause real harm to keep, should sometimes yield to a greater good; blindly honouring a reckless vow is stubbornness, not integrity. Yet these exceptions are rare, and the person who treats them as loopholes soon becomes untrustworthy in the ordinary cases that matter most.

The wiser attitude, therefore, is to promise carefully and then keep faithfully — thinking twice before committing, but regarding a commitment made as a genuine obligation.

In conclusion, while a few extreme situations may excuse a broken promise, the habit of keeping one's word remains among the most important qualities anyone can possess. It is, quite simply, what allows human beings to depend on one another.

subTopics.title: 毕业致辞·责任的分量
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：It is my pleasure and privilege to welcome you here today——校长的毕业致辞把责任比作船锚：a ship without an anchor is at the mercy of the waves; likewise, a person who has no sense of responsibility……

prompts.task: 你作为毕业生代表将在高中毕业典礼上用英文发言，主题为'责任'。请写一篇发言稿，内容包括：1. 回顾成长；2. 谈谈责任的意义；3. 对同学们的寄语。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Honoured teachers and fellow students, it is my privilege to speak on this special occasion.

Three years ago we arrived as nervous Senior 1 students; today we sit here as confident young adults, ready to walk out into the world. If there is one thing our school has taught us, it is a sense of responsibility. A ship without an anchor is at the mercy of the waves and winds; likewise, a person with no sense of responsibility drifts through life. Responsibility to our families, our society and our own promises is what gives our journey direction.

So as we say goodbye, let us carry this anchor with us. Wherever we go, may we be people the world can count on. Thank you!
vocabHints: at the mercy of the waves and winds
people the world can count on

prompts.task: Some people believe that young people today have a weaker sense of responsibility than previous generations. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
It is a familiar complaint that today's young people care less about duty than their parents and grandparents did. I disagree with this claim: young people's sense of responsibility has not weakened but changed shape, and in some ways it has grown.

Those who criticise the young usually point to surface habits — dependence on phones, later independence from parents, or a reluctance to take traditional jobs. Yet these reflect a transformed world rather than lost character. Young people stay in education longer and leave home later largely because the economy demands it, not because they refuse to grow up. What looks like irresponsibility is often simply a different path to adulthood.

In fact, on many measures the young show responsibility their elders rarely did. They volunteer in large numbers, lead campaigns on climate change and social justice, and hold institutions to account through the very technology critics blame. A generation that organises to protect the planet its parents damaged can hardly be called indifferent to duty. Their sense of responsibility simply extends beyond the household to global concerns.

It would be naive to pretend every young person is diligent; every generation contains the lazy and the selfish. But the same was true in the past, which nostalgia conveniently forgets.

In conclusion, I do not accept that young people are less responsible than before. Their duties look different — shaped by new pressures and new causes — but the underlying willingness to care for others and to act rightly remains as strong as ever, and is perhaps directed at a wider world than earlier generations imagined.

subTopics.title: 勇于担当·别急于责怪他人
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：shoulder the burden、be quick to blame others、feel guilty about、be ready to admit——真正的担当，是先分析问题、承认过错，而不是急着把责任推给别人。

prompts.task: 你班一次小组作业出了差错，有同学互相指责。请你就'如何对待失误'为班会写一篇英文短文，内容包括：1. 现象与看法；2. 你的建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
After our group project went wrong last week, the first thing many of us did was to look for someone to blame. But pointing fingers solved nothing.

In my view, when something goes wrong, we should not be quick to blame others. Instead, we should calmly analyse the problem, and if it is indeed our own fault, be ready to admit it. Shouldering our share of the responsibility, rather than shifting it onto teammates, is what holds a group together. There is no shame in making mistakes; the real shame lies in refusing to own them.

A person willing to say "that was my fault" is not weaker, but stronger — and far easier to trust.
vocabHints: shoulder our share of the responsibility

prompts.task: When something goes wrong, some people think the most important thing is to find who is responsible, while others believe it is better to focus on finding a solution. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
When a plan fails or an accident happens, people react in two ways: some rush to identify who is at fault, while others concentrate on putting things right. Both instincts have value, but in my opinion finding a solution should usually come first, with the question of blame handled carefully and later.

There is a genuine case for establishing responsibility. If no one is ever held accountable, careless behaviour goes unchecked and the same mistakes recur; identifying the cause of a failure often means identifying the person whose actions produced it. In serious matters — a medical error, a financial fraud — determining who was responsible is essential to justice and to prevention.

Yet an obsession with blame frequently makes things worse. When people fear punishment, they hide mistakes rather than report them, so problems grow in the dark; teams waste energy defending themselves instead of repairing the damage. Focusing first on a solution keeps everyone working toward the same goal and creates the honesty in which real causes can later be understood. The best organisations, tellingly, investigate failures to learn, not merely to punish.

The wisest approach therefore combines the two in the right order: fix the immediate problem, then examine calmly what went wrong and how to prevent it, treating individual fault as one factor rather than the whole story.

In conclusion, while responsibility must not be ignored, a healthy response to failure looks forward before it looks back. Solving the problem restores what was lost; assigning blame, done wisely and without cruelty, helps ensure it does not happen again.

subTopics.title: 承认错误的勇气
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心词块：bow one's head、admit a mistake、not pretend——低头认错从来不是懦弱，而是一种需要勇气的责任。

prompts.task: 你的朋友 Tom 因为不小心弄坏了同学的东西，却不敢承认，为此十分苦恼。请你用英文给他写一封信，内容包括：1. 表达理解；2. 建议他勇于承认；3. 鼓励。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Tom,

I can tell that hiding what happened has been weighing on you. It is never easy to admit a mistake, and I understand why you have hesitated.

But pretending that nothing is wrong only makes things heavier. If you go to your classmate, bow your head honestly and say sorry, most people will forgive far more readily than you fear. Offering to repair or replace what was broken will show that you mean it. Admitting a fault is not a sign of weakness; it takes real courage, and it sets your own mind free.

You are a good person who made a small mistake. Own it, and you will feel lighter at once. I'm with you.

Yours,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Some people think that admitting one's mistakes is a sign of weakness, while others believe it is a sign of strength. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
When people make errors, they face a choice: confess or conceal. Some regard admitting a mistake as an embarrassing weakness; others see it as a mark of genuine strength. Having considered both, I firmly believe that owning one's faults requires and reveals strength, though I understand why it can feel like the opposite.

The view that admission is weakness is easy to understand. Confessing an error exposes us to criticism, damages our image and can carry real costs — a lost job, a lower grade, a bruised reputation. In competitive settings, showing fallibility may look like handing rivals an advantage, so people instinctively hide behind excuses or blame others.

Yet this reasoning mistakes short-term self-protection for strength. Admitting a mistake takes courage precisely because it is hard: it means facing discomfort honestly rather than fleeing into denial. It also builds something concealment destroys — trust. A leader who says "I was wrong" earns more respect than one who never concedes anything, because people sense the honesty behind it. Practically, too, mistakes acknowledged can be corrected and learned from, while mistakes hidden fester and repeat. The truly weak response is the cover-up that protects pride at the cost of growth.

In my view, therefore, the strength lies in admission, not denial. The person who can say "that was my fault" without collapsing possesses a security that defensiveness only imitates.

In conclusion, although confessing errors exposes us and can feel like weakness, it is in fact a form of courage. Those who can own their mistakes grow wiser and earn deeper trust than those who never dare to.
